subject: Order form — output ownership, training opt-out & feedback license
messages:
From: Maya Shah <m.shah@brightbridge.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightbridge.com, legal@brightbridge.com
Date: 2028-06-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Order form review — output rights & training opt-out

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — excited to move forward. Procurement has a couple of legal points we need to close before we can get internal sign-off:

1) Output ownership: we need explicit confirmation that BrightBridge will retain exclusive ownership of derivative outputs for our product (we'll provide prompts/data). We're ok with Redwood retaining rights to improve its service, but we need language that limits Redwood from productizing BrightBridge-specific output.

2) Training/data use: BrightBridge must be able to opt out of model retraining using our customer-provided data and prompt corpus. If opt-out is not an option, procurement needs a defined commercial tradeoff (e.g., surcharge).

3) Feedback license: BrightBridge can agree to a limited feedback license for bug fixes and safety improvements, but we want assurances that feedback is aggregated and not used to re-create customer-specific outputs.

Can you share a redline and your recommended path (order form addendum vs MSA amendment)? We need a legal-stamped version for our vendors gate by end of week (June 7) to hit Q3 procurement cycles.

Attaching the procurement checklist separately (sending via procurement@).

Appreciate a quick path here — cc'ing our legal and procurement contacts who will be co-reviewing.

Best,
Maya Shah
Head of Procurement, BrightBridge
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Shah <m.shah@brightbridge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-02T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Order form review — output rights & training opt-out

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear summary and timeline. We can get you a legal-stamped redline but want to align on practical options so we don't bounce too many iterations. Below are three pragmatic paths — I'll attach a drafted redline and a short playbook for procurement.

Option A (default, no charge):
- Output: Customer retains ownership of content they provide and outputs generated from their prompts; Redwood retains the right to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry to operate and improve the service.
- Training: Redwood may use de-identified usage signals for model tuning (operational improvements).
- Feedback: Redwood receives a non-exclusive, perpetual, worldwide feedback license limited to improving the platform (aggregated/synthetic).

Option B (opt-out for training; moderate fee):
- Same as A but BrightBridge can opt out of data being included in any model retraining pipelines. We propose a monthly opt-out fee (see attached pricing sheet) to cover the operational and opportunity cost.

Option C (strict training prohibition; one-time commercial):
- BrightBridge grants no training rights for any data or outputs and Redwood accepts a one-time commercial concession (one-time fee) plus contractual assurances around segmentation. This is typically practical for private/on-prem or very large commitments.

Recommendations and next steps:
- For Hosted / standard Order Form customers we most commonly sign Option A or B. Option C is possible but requires Legal + Procurement + Sales approval (and procurement budget sign-off).
- I'll route the attached redline to Legal (laura) and Sales Ops (ben/jordan) now for fast review. If you confirm preferred option, we'll produce a version for signature (DocuSign) by June 6 to meet your June 7 deadline.

Attached: BB_OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx (redline), training-optout-pricing.xlsx, redwood-feedback-license-draft.pdf

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-02T11:09:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Order form review — output rights & training opt-out (BrightBridge) — internal review

Team — forwarding BrightBridge ask. Quick notes:
- BrightBridge explicitly requests exclusive ownership of derivative outputs for their product. This is heavier than typical — we usually accept customer output ownership but reserve rights to aggregate and improve models.
- Pricing signal: they indicate they will accept an opt-out for training with a commercial concession. Procurement deadline is June 7.

Questions for Legal / Sales:
1) Is the proposed "aggregated feedback" carveout in our redline sufficient to prevent reuse of customer-specific outputs? Laura, can you confirm wording that prevents reconstitution/replay?
2) Operationally, can we tag customer data to ensure no retraining pipelines include it by default? Ben/Jordan — confirm with infra/ops if tagging+segregation is feasible within 2 weeks for a hosted customer. If not, what are the gating items?
3) If we require a commercial fee for opt-out, what's the recommended pricing band (monthly vs one-time)? Tentative: training-optout-pricing.xlsx attached for reference.

I propose we produce two deliverables for BrightBridge: (1) Order Form addendum with Option B spelled out for hosted customers, (2) MSA amendment template for Option C (private/on-prem). If Legal signs off, I'll get the DocuSign link ready.

Thanks — Hannah
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Shah <m.shah@brightbridge.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, legal@brightbridge.com
Date: 2028-06-03T08:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Order form review — output rights & training opt-out

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask and patience. Quick update from our side after Legal & Product review: we've accepted Option B for BrightBridge (Order Form addendum) with the following clarified points:

- Output ownership: BrightBridge retains ownership of outputs derived from customer-provided prompts and data. Redwood will not assert ownership over BrightBridge-specific outputs.
- Training opt-out: BrightBridge can opt out of inclusion in Redwood retraining pipelines. We will implement a data-tagging exclusion and operationalize exclusion within 14 business days of the signed addendum.
- Fee: For Hosted customers we are proposing a training-opt-out surcharge of $12,000/month (see attached workbook). For Dedicated/Private deployments we can offer a one-time fee alternative; details can be discussed if you prefer that path.
- Feedback license: The redline limits Redwood to a non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual license to use feedback only to improve the Redwood service. Usage will be aggregated and processed to prevent re-creation or productization of BrightBridge-specific outputs.

I've attached the legal-stamped redline (BB_OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx) and the pricing workbook. Next step: if this aligns with your procurement team, we'll send a DocuSign packet today (link below) and schedule a short ops call to confirm tagging/segregation timeline.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/BB-097
Ops call: propose 2028-06-04T15:00Z — let us know if that works.

Respectfully,
Ben Carter
Head, Commercial Contracts (acting), Redwood Inference
